neckTest.title: The neck check
neckTest.body: Slip two fingers behind the baby's neck. Warm and dry means just right. Damp or sweaty means too warm. Cold means add a layer.

wool.title: Why wool?
wool.body: Wool keeps warmth even when damp, and lets skin breathe. For the youngest, wool is often safer than cotton or synthetics.

newborn.title: Newborns under 3 months
newborn.body: Tiny babies struggle to regulate temperature. Keep outings under 30 minutes in cold weather. Check the neck and back often.

disclaimer.title: A note
disclaimer.body: Babyora is a guide, not a verdict. You know your baby best. Speak to a health professional if something feels off.

rain.moderate: Moderate rain — pop a rain cover over the stroller.

ageWarning.title: Babyora is built for 0–2 years
ageWarning.body: You can still use the app, but suggestions are most accurate for the youngest babies.

common.neckCheck: Slip two fingers behind the baby's neck — warm and dry means just right.

sleep.warmRoom: Bedroom feels warm — air it out a bit or use a lighter sleep sack.
sleep.coolRoom: Bedroom feels cool — nudge the heating up a notch.
sleep.safeSleep: A sleep sack is safest. No loose blankets or pillows in the cot.
sleep.newbornBackSleep: The little one sleeps safest on their back. Check in on the neck now and then.

rain.heavy: It's bucketing down — maybe a shorter outing or a fully covered stroller?
rain.drizzle: Light drizzle — the canopy usually handles it. Feel for damp now and then.

wind.strong: Brisk wind today — shield the face and keep the outing short.

notes.humidCold: Damp cold feels colder than the thermometer says — an extra layer is wise.

newborn.thermoregulation: Newborns regulate temperature poorly — check neck and back often.
newborn.coldShortTrip: Keep the trip short in the cold — half an hour max. Dab thick cream on the cheeks.
newborn.coldWindWait: Wind and cold are hard on the little ones — consider waiting until the wind drops.
newborn.heatTolerance: Newborns handle heat poorly — short outings and shade matter most.
newborn.coldLimit: Babies under 3 months: max 30 min outside in freezing temps. Check neck and back often.

stroller.noBlanket: Never drape a blanket over the canopy — it traps heat.
stroller.warmPouchBlanket: Use either a foot muff or a blanket, not both — it heats up fast.
stroller.mildShade: Mild day in the stroller — seek shade and check the neck now and then.
stroller.sunTent: Sun on the canopy turns the stroller into a tent. An airy sun sail works better.
stroller.outdoorSleepFrost: Outdoor naps in frost: check every half hour. A down muff alone isn't always enough.

carrier.noDownInside: Your body warms the baby — skip down innermost, it gets clammy.
carrier.insideJacket: Baby is inside your jacket — you bring the warmth, skip the outer layer.

outdoorPlay.coldKindergarten: Properly cold — check what nursery recommends for outdoor play today.
outdoorPlay.coldBreakLayer: When you take a break: add a layer. Kids cool down fast when standing still.

cold.frostCream: Dab thick cream on the cheeks half an hour before heading out.
cold.frostWindCheck: Watch the cheeks and ears underway — white patches mean it's freezing.
cold.longTripBreak: Long trip in the cold — plan an indoor break to warm up.

sun.youngShade: Sun is lovely, but keep the little one in shade. Sunscreen waits until 6 months.
sun.olderHatSunscreen: Sun hat and sunscreen on what's exposed. Check the UV — snow and mountains can surprise.
sun.uvHigh: Strong sun today — stay in shade between 11 and 3.

safety.carSeatThickSuit: In the car seat: take off the thick suit, tighten the harness, lay the suit over as a blanket.

heat.extreme: Very hot today — never alone in the car, plenty to drink, plenty of shade.

peak.overheating79mo: Babies 7–9 months produce the most body heat. Use fewer layers than usual, check the neck often.

research.overheatingPeak: Babies 7–9 months produce the most body heat. Use fewer layers than usual, check the neck often.
research.newbornColdLimit: Babies under 3 months: max 30 min outside in freezing temps. Check neck and back often.

explanations.ACTIVE_CHILD_LESS_INSULATION: Your child will be active — fewer garments prevent overheating and sweat.
explanations.RESTING_CHILD_MORE_INSULATION: Your child is mostly still — an extra warm garment keeps body heat in.
explanations.RAIN_REQUIRES_SHELL: Rain expected — a waterproof shell keeps the garments underneath dry.
explanations.WIND_REQUIRES_SHELL: The wind calls for a windproof shell.
explanations.WOOL_PREFERENCE_APPLIED: Wool is chosen where it fits, as you prefer.
explanations.WOOL_AVOIDED: Wool has been left out — fully capable alternatives are used instead.
explanations.FLEECE_FAST_DRYING: Fleece is chosen because it dries quickly and works well under a shell.
explanations.WICKING_SYNTHETIC_FOR_ACTIVITY: Technical base layers wick sweat away when your child is moving.
explanations.COTTON_ONLY_WARM_DRY: Cotton is a good choice when it is warm, dry and calm.
explanations.AGE_APPROPRIATE_GARMENT_FORM: The garment shape matches your child’s age.
explanations.CALIBRATION_WARMER: Adjusted slightly warmer based on your feedback.
explanations.CALIBRATION_COOLER: Adjusted slightly lighter based on your feedback.
